checks.title: Plain HTTP requests redirect to HTTPS
checks.why: Without a redirect, a visitor who types the bare domain sends the whole session over plaintext, including any cookie set without the Secure flag.
checks.action: Configure the web server or CDN to answer HTTP with a permanent redirect to the HTTPS URL, and enable HSTS once you are confident.

verify.manual: Open the site over plain HTTP in a private window and confirm the browser lands on the HTTPS URL before any content renders.

checks.title: A favicon is served
checks.why: Browsers request a favicon on every page load. When it is missing the site logs a 404 on each visit and shows a blank tab icon in bookmarks and history.
checks.action: Add a favicon at the site root, and reference the sizes you need from the document head.

verify.cmd: ls favicon.ico favicon.svg public/favicon.ico static/favicon.ico 2>/dev/null | head -5
verify.expect: At least one favicon file is listed.

checks.title: Open Graph tags are present on shareable pages
checks.why: Without them a shared link renders as a bare URL with no title, description or image, which measurably reduces click-through from chat and social apps.
checks.action: Add og:title, og:description, og:image and og:url to the document head of every page meant to be shared.

verify.expect: At least one template declares Open Graph tags.

checks.title: Security response headers are served
checks.why: Without them a browser has no instruction to block framing, to stop guessing content types, or to withhold the referring URL, so three whole classes of attack stay available for the sake of a few response headers.
checks.action: Serve Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and Strict-Transport-Security from the application, the web server or the CDN, whichever sits closest to the user.

verify.manual: Load the deployed site and inspect the response headers on the main document, then confirm each of the four is present with a value you chose deliberately.

checks.title: A robots file exists and does not block the whole site
checks.why: A robots file copied from a staging environment usually disallows everything, and it will keep the production site out of search results silently for as long as nobody thinks to look at it.
checks.action: Publish a robots file that allows the pages you want indexed, disallows the ones you do not, and points at your sitemap.

verify.expect: A robots file exists and does not disallow the entire site, unless keeping it unindexed is deliberate.
